title: Clopen refinements are cofinal among pointed etale neighbourhoods
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $C$ be a commutative $K$-algebra, and put $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that for every prime $z\subset C$ the structural map $K\to C_z$ is an isomorphism, where $C_z$ denotes localization at the complement of $z$. Assume also that clopen subsets form a basis of $E$: for every open $U\subseteq E$ and $z\in U$ there is an open and closed $W$ with $z\in W\subseteq U$. Fix any geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$ [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over $z$. For every pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar z$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], there are a clopen neighbourhood $W\subseteq E$ of $z$ and an $E$-morphism $b:W\to V$ satisfying $b\circ\bar z_W=\bar v$, where $\bar z_W$ is the unique factorization of $\bar z$ through $W$. Given two clopen neighbourhoods $W_1,W_2$ of $z$ and pointed $E$-morphisms $b_i:W_i\to V$, there is a clopen neighbourhood $W_3\subseteq W_1\cap W_2$ of $z$ on which $b_1$ and $b_2$ agree. Thus the clopen pointed neighbourhoods form an initial subsystem [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] of the pointed etale neighbourhoods. Each clopen $W$ is $D(e)=\operatorname{Spec}C_e$ for an idempotent $e\in C$, with its open-subscheme structure, where $C_e$ is localization at $e$.

proof.text: For any clopen $W\subseteq E$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] gives an idempotent $e\in C$ with $W=D(e)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], this open subscheme is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}C_e$. This proves the final assertion, including $W=\varnothing$ with $e=0$ and $W=E$ with $e=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], each such open neighbourhood of $z$, pointed by the factorization of $\bar z$, is a pointed etale neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition; schemes.tex Tags 01I3 and 01HV; morphisms.tex Tag 02GP

proof.text: Write $\lambda:C\to C_z$ for localization. The ring map $a:C\to\Omega$ defining $\bar z$ has kernel $z$, so $a(s)\ne0$ and hence is a unit for every $s\notin z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property], it extends uniquely to $\gamma:C_z\to\Omega$. The structural isomorphism $\alpha:K\xrightarrow{\sim}C_z$ in the hypothesis gives a field embedding $\beta=\gamma\alpha:K\to\Omega$. With $t=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha^{-1}\lambda):\operatorname{Spec}K\to E$, contravariance of the spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $\bar z=t\circ\operatorname{Spec}\beta$. In particular $\gamma$ is injective, since $C_z$ is the field $K$.

Let $p:V\to E$ and $\bar v$ be the given pointed etale neighbourhood. Apply [lem-exc-etale-lift-separably-closed-factorization] with $L=K$, $\beta$ and $t$ from step 2: there is $y:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$ with $p y=t$ and $y\circ\operatorname{Spec}\beta=\bar v$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink], choose an affine open etale refinement $j:A=\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ containing the image of $\bar v$. The one-point source of $y$ has that same image, so $y$ restricts to $y_A:\operatorname{Spec}K\to A$; its map on structure sheaves is just the restriction of that of $y$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $j y_A=y$ and $y_A\circ\operatorname{Spec}\beta=\bar v_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $B$ is finitely presented over $C$. The affine correspondence gives a $C$-algebra map $h:B\to C_z$ for $y_A\circ\operatorname{Spec}\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}C_z\to A$ (its composite to $E$ is $t\circ\operatorname{Spec}\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}\lambda$).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations] with $P=C$ and $S=C\setminus z$. This is a small filtered diagram (the index is a subset of the set $C$), with objects $C_s$, colimit $C_z$, and $C$-algebra transition and cocone maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] to the finitely presented $C$-algebra $B$ and $h$. It supplies $s\notin z$ and a $C$-algebra map $h_s:B\to C_s$ whose composite to $C_z$ is $h$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], this is an $E$-morphism $d:D(s)\to A$. Its composite with the factorization of $\bar z$ through $D(s)$ equals $\bar v_A$: both ring maps $B\to\Omega$ are $B\xrightarrow{h}C_z\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Omega$.

Since $s\notin z$, $z\in D(s)$. The assumed clopen basis supplies $z\in W\subseteq D(s)$ with $W$ clopen. Define $b$ as the restriction of $j\circ d$ to $W$. Open-subscheme restriction [def-weil-open-immersion] means restriction of the underlying continuous map and of its structure sheaf maps, so it preserves the base equation and the marked-point equation of step 4. Therefore $b:W\to V$ has $b\circ\bar z_W=\bar v$. This proves the existence assertion.

proof.text: For equalization, let $b_i:W_i\to V$ be the two pointed maps. Their values at $z$ are the common image $v$ of $\bar v$. Choose an affine open etale refinement $A=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq V$ containing $v$ using [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink]. The intersection $O=W_1\cap W_2\cap b_1^{-1}(A)\cap b_2^{-1}(A)$ is open in $E$ and contains $z$ (the inverse images are first open in $W_i$, which are open in $E$). Choose a clopen $z\in W_0\subseteq O$. By step 1 write $W_0=D(e)=\operatorname{Spec}C_e$. Restricting maps and sheaf maps [def-weil-open-immersion] gives two $E$-maps $W_0\to A$, hence $C$-algebra maps $u_1,u_2:B\to C_e$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], choose a finite presentation of $B$ over $C$, and denote its algebra generators by $x_1,\ldots,x_n$.

For each generator put $\delta_j=u_1(x_j)-u_2(x_j)=a_j/e^{r_j}$ in $C_e$. Pointedness says its image in $\Omega$ is zero. Since $e

otin z$ with $t_j a_j=0$ in $C$. Put $t=\prod_{j=1}^n t_j$ (the empty product is $1$). Then $t
otin z$ and $ta_j=0$ for every $j$. Choose a clopen $z\in W_3\subseteq W_0\cap D(t)$, and write $W_3=D(f)$ by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], the restriction maps $C_e=\mathcal O_E(D(e))	o\mathcal O_E(W_3)=C_f$ and $C_t=\mathcal O_E(D(t))	o C_f$ carry $e^{-1}$ and $t^{-1}$ to inverses of $e$ and $t$. Thus every $\delta_j$ restricts to zero. The two $C$-algebra maps $B	o C_f$ agree on $C$ and on all the $x_j$, hence on every polynomial in these generators and therefore on $B$. The affine correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] shows $b_1|_{W_3}=b_2|_{W_3}$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C_z$ be the category of clopen neighbourhoods of $z$, with arrows the inclusions, and send it to $\mathcal N_{\bar z}$ using the inherited marked points [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. These objects and arrows are etale-site objects and arrows by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. For each $(V,\bar v)$ the category of pairs $(W,b:W\to V)$ is nonempty by step 5. For any two such pairs, step 7 supplies inclusions $W_1\leftarrow W_3\to W_2$ commuting with their maps to $V$. Thus any two objects of this category are joined by a zigzag, so it is connected. These are exactly conditions (1) and (2) of initiality in [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit]: every such comma category is nonempty and connected. The explicit existence, equalization and idempotent assertions have all been established.
